newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty off vs basket, depos inch upward.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty off vs basket, depos inch upward.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed Tuesday's session weaker against the basket of currencies, pushed down by a late currency buying-trend surrounding possible small-scale sales of Polish T-bills by a foreign investor, dealers said.
"Someone was purchasing dollars today, perhaps a foreign investor who sold T-bills in secondary trade," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.
However, dealers said that for most of the day the zloty inched upward as banks sold dollars to take advantage of the U.S. unit's rally against major currencies after the U.S. fired missles on Iraq.
"The zloty was pushed down on the back of one big order, but the general trend was to weaken," said Pawel Kowalski, forex dealer at Creditanstalt SA in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 1.71/1.67 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Monday's close at 1.78/1.76 percent.
It was at 2.7495/05 to the dollar, down from Monday's 2.7433/38 and at 1.8492/02 to the mark, flat from 1.8491/97.
The one-day deposit market was basically balanced but rates rose slightly as there were some banks with surplus money and there was no cash outflows from central bank drainage operations on Tuesday.
Overnight rates were at 18.70/19.10 percent, up from 18.5/19.0 percent at opening and tomorrow/next rates closed at 18.8/19.2 percent, up from 18.5/19.0 percent.
The central bank drained 323 million zlotys off the market for 14-days at a flat average rate of 19.05 percent and it allocated 500 million zlotys of its NBP-bills on Tuesday.

The average yield of the 91-day NBP-bill was 19.25 percent against an average yield of 18.73 percent for a comparable 13-week T-bill sold at last Monday's primary tender. The 273-day average yield rose 0.02 point to 19.83 percent.
